proposed_from.topic: Exact quotient and nuisance-minimax inference for off-target exposure levels in discrete IV models. Let finite randomized Z have m arms, binary Y, and X=T union C. Require well-defined Z-excluded Y_t only for t in T; allow unrestricted X(z), and fully saturated arm-specific responses R_{c,z} for c in C. Prove that the sharp identified set for law(Y_T) depends only on skeleton cells p(X=t,Y=y|Z=z), equals the image of the reduced type simplex (T union {star})^Z times {0,1}^T, and is independent of |C| by an explicit right inverse. Conditional on arm counts, factor the full experiment into skeleton counts and a variation-independent nuisance allocation; for every convex loss prove the precise nuisance-minimax reduction R_q(delta0)<=sup_eta R_(q,eta)(delta), not pointwise domination. Adapt Song et al.'s method-of-types KL region for simultaneous finite-sample coverage of the entire reduced identified set, including endpoint kinks; state calibration and computation as independent of |C| but exponential in m and |T|, and prove feasible-law Hoffman/dual excess-width bounds plus a regular-face n^-1/2 lower bound. Verify by exact enumeration the Z={0,1},T={a,b},C={c} witness with z0 masses (a,0)=1/2,(c,1)=1/2 and z1 masses (a,0)=1/2,(c,0)=1/2: saturated responses give E[Y_b-Y_a] bounds [-1/2,1], while a common excluded Y_c gives [0,1]. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: represent reduced atoms r by x_z in T union {star} and y_T; the incidence map A records target cells and star mass and B records law(Y_T). Refine each star coordinate independently using eta_z(c,y)=p(c,y|z)/s(z,star), with a boundary convention at zero star mass, to obtain a full-law right inverse. Conditional multinomial likelihood then splits into a (2|T|+1)-cell skeleton factor and an eta_z allocation factor. For d=2|T|+1 use rho_z=[log(m/alpha)+(d-1)log(n_z+1)]/n_z in D(hat s_z||s_z), followed by reduced-polytope projection. Credit Gabriel et al. for finite coarsening cases, Song et al. for categorical-IV KL projection, Boushehrian et al. for exponential target-dimension limits, Sachs et al. for response LPs, and Levis et al. for active-facet inference. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: prove the simplex/equality-system Hoffman statement for scalar support functions and keep every novelty claim confined to target-specific exclusion quotienting, nuisance-minimax equivalence, arbitrary finite cardinalities, and |C|-free inference. EARLY KILL TEST: enumerate the 36 reduced columns and corresponding 144 saturated full types for m=2,|T|=2, compare random support functions across multiple |C|, and require the displayed bounds exactly.

seed_details.title: Target-specific exclusion quotient with a saturated off-target right inverse
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction and Results 1--3 on pp. 2--4 and 13--16, the response-function proof boundary on pp. 13--14, and the Discussion on pp. 22--23 of arXiv:2401.17735 were read.
seed_details.anchor_quote: Investigating if this pattern extends to higher levels of the exposure ... and if it can be proven for arbitrary levels.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The low-cardinality vertex-enumeration argument does not supply a surjection from arbitrary off-target refinements to a target-potential-outcome fiber. The first changed step is to collapse every off-target realized exposure to \(\star\), then explicitly lift each reduced atom by armwise conditional allocations \(\eta_z(c,y)\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for target-specific exclusion, off-target exposure quotients, arbitrary-cardinality coarsening, and categorical instrumental-variable response types located no theorem beyond the low-cardinality cases and the fully excluded categorical model.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Song et al. because their Theorem 1 already handles arbitrary finite categorical treatments.
seed_details.rebuttal: Song et al. define excluded potential outcomes for every treatment category; the proposed model deliberately has no common \(Y_c\) for \(c\in\mathcal C\), and equality with the reduced image requires a new right inverse at positive and zero \(\star\)-mass.

seed_details.title: Nuisance-minimax equivalence of the full and skeleton experiments
seed_details.anchor_opened: The full-data categorical setup in Section 2, the identification construction in Theorem 1 and Supplement S2, the multinomial experiment in Section 6, and the Conclusion of arXiv:2405.09510v6 were read; Blackwell's publisher record was opened as the method thread.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The skeleton is not sufficient for \((q,\eta)\), so ordinary Rao--Blackwell pointwise domination is false. The first changed step is to factor the conditional multinomial likelihood and average a full-data rule with a fixed allocation kernel before taking \(\sup_\eta\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining categorical instrumental variables, skeleton counts, nuisance minimaxity, variation-independent allocations, and comparison of experiments found no occupied target--method pair.
seed_details.red_team: The off-target labels are ancillary, so discarding them is an elementary sufficiency argument.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their conditional distribution depends on \(\eta\), making them non-ancillary for the full parameter and preventing a parameter-free pointwise Rao--Blackwell improvement; only the nuisance-supremum risk comparison survives.

seed_details.title: Finite-sample projection for the entire reduced identified set
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Theorem 1 and Eq. 8, Section 6 and Theorem 4, the sufficiency construction in Supplement S2, and the Conclusion of arXiv:2405.09510v6 were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Song et al. calibrate the full \(KM\)-cell arm law under exclusion for every treatment. The first changed step is to establish the target-only quotient before concentration, then project an armwise \(d=2|\mathcal T|+1\) method-of-types region to a union of complete reduced fibers.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for simultaneous finite-sample coverage of a target-potential-outcome identified set under partial exclusion and for calibration independent of off-target support found no direct result.
seed_details.red_team: This is only Song et al.'s confidence program after replacing its alphabet size.
seed_details.rebuttal: Replacing the alphabet is valid only after proving equality of the saturated full and reduced identified images; the resulting event covers the whole set at facet switches and is uniform over unrestricted off-target allocations.

seed_details.title: Global feasible-fiber and support-value modulus for the reduced incidence system
seed_details.anchor_opened: The main theorem, its active-halfspace proof on pp. 263--264, and the discussion of computable constants on pp. 264--265 were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Hoffman's theorem controls distance to one fixed inequality system. The first changed step is a uniform restriction to compatible right-hand sides of the simplex equality fiber \(Aq=s\), followed by the stochastic target map \(B\) and support-function duality.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for Hoffman constants, response-function instrumental-variable fibers, support-function perturbations, and off-target cardinality found generic polyhedral sensitivity results but no target-specific quotient modulus.
seed_details.red_team: The desired bound is a one-line corollary of the 1952 Hoffman lemma.
seed_details.rebuttal: The publishable content is the compatible-simplex fiber formulation, a finite active-system certificate, passage to all scalar support values, and its combination with the reduced KL region; generic theory alone does not state this \(|\mathcal C|\)-free causal modulus.

seed_details.title: Minimax phase diagram for regular faces and target-IV facet kinks
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Theorems 1--3, the margin construction in Sections 4--5, proof appendices, and the Discussion of arXiv:2301.12106v4 were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Levis et al. obtain root-\(n\) inference under a margin condition or conservative smoothing for binary-IV formulas. The first changed step is to analyze the finite dual fan of the reduced arbitrary-cardinality LP and build local alternatives that cross a nonunique dual face.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches joining categorical-IV support endpoints, active-facet minimax rates, and off-target quotienting found regularized affine-model inference in Gafarov but no sharp target-IV kink phase diagram.
seed_details.red_team: Gafarov already gives uniform Gaussian inference for polygonal identified sets.
seed_details.rebuttal: Gafarov regularizes a generic affine model; it neither derives the exact local minimax law at target-IV dual ties nor proves invariance to arbitrary off-target refinements.

seed_details.title: Critical-violation frontier between a common off-target outcome and saturated arm responses
seed_details.anchor_opened: Results 1--3 and the Discussion of arXiv:2401.17735 were read, including the distinction between well-defined, ill-defined, and instrument-contaminated exposure levels.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to replace equality of off-target responses across arms by a total-variation budget \(\delta\), optimize target support values over the resulting coupling polytope, and derive the first \(\delta\) at which a sign conclusion changes.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for critical-\(\delta\) sensitivity of off-target exclusion in categorical instrumental-variable bounds found qualitative contamination analyses but no derived frontier.
seed_details.red_team: The sensitivity curve is a routine parametric LP in \(\delta\).
seed_details.rebuttal: A useful result would require a sharp piecewise-linear envelope and a dual characterization of the critical \(\delta\), not merely resolving the LP on a grid.

seed_details.title: Covariate-conditional quotient and efficient regular-face endpoint estimation
seed_details.anchor_opened: The covariate-assisted Balke--Pearl setup, margin condition, influence-function expansion in Theorem 2, smooth approximation in Theorem 3, and Discussion were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to prove the quotient pointwise in covariates and then differentiate an integrated reduced support value through its active dual basis.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for covariate-assisted categorical instrumental-variable bounds under target-only exclusion located binary fully excluded endpoint theory but no conditional quotient or efficiency bound.
seed_details.red_team: This is a mechanical conditional version of the finite quotient.
seed_details.rebuttal: The identification step is pointwise, but efficient estimation requires a new influence function for a covariate-indexed LP value and a margin condition on dual-basis switches.

seed_details.title: Closed nonredundant inequalities for the reduced target-law polytope
seed_details.anchor_opened: Theorem 1, the Strassen sufficiency argument in Supplement S2, and the nonredundancy analysis in Sections 4--5 of arXiv:2405.09510v6 were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The proposed first step was to treat \(\star\) as an observed category with a deterministic response and eliminate its potential outcome from Song et al.'s inequalities.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method search showed that this inequality family follows directly once the quotient theorem is known.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Song et al. by adding a deterministic \(\star\) category.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the inequality representation considered in isolation.

seed_details.title: Sharper Chernoff calibration on the reduced alphabet
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Theorem 1 and its induction proof, the Chernoff inversion, and the Conclusion of arXiv:2003.08614 were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The proposed first step was to substitute \(d=2|\mathcal T|+1\) into the polynomial moment-generating-function bound after quotienting.
seed_details.destination_search: The method paper already proves the required uniform multinomial inequality for every finite alphabet size.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Guo and Richardson because their theorem is alphabet-generic.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds; only the preceding quotient is new, so this cannot stand as a seed.
